findings.text: blocking: the prior-head boundary-flux lag-one cells are 0.0852 on white and 0.4537 on drift (per-slice-span fraction), while the corrected rows at :40-:41 carry 0.099 and 0.549 (fraction of the generating state's fixed span, which is what analyse.py:65 computes and what the r-20261119 summary.json records), and the r-20261115 arm's own summary.json records 0.1186 and 0.1866 for those same rows, so one column mixes two conventions and the corrected-versus-prior comparison the table exists for compares unlike statistics.

blocking: the prior-head white boundary-flux cell carries 0.0852 under the same mixed convention as :46, where the arm's own summary.json records 0.1186, so a reader comparing the white arms reads a 0.099-versus-0.0852 difference that the arms' own summaries do not support.

blocking: the added method sentence says the table "keeps the fraction form the arm's own summary records" and that the raw-Wb alternative reads 0.1186 and 0.1866 "because the span varies slice to slice", but a constant divisor leaves a correlation unchanged so raw Wb and the fixed-span fraction are the same 0.1186/0.1866, and the cells at :44 and :46 are the per-slice-span variant the sentence says the table does not use; the sentence therefore cannot be used to reproduce the cells it was added to source.

non-blocking: the sentence runs on from "and the drift is" into "Every lag-one figure ...", dropping the clause about where the drift is carried that the replaced text ended with, so the published record carries a visibly broken sentence.

non-blocking: the sentence describes the axis lag-one as "the mean over the two coordinates", but analyse.py:30-37 computes lag_one by averaging the table's two per-coordinate correlations, and correlating the mean-coordinate series gives -0.0682 on white and 0.4659 on drift rather than the -0.018 and 0.441 the table states.

non-blocking: the wall assertion compares the file against an expected array built by calling wall_units_from_ids, the same function wall_npz calls, and the bespoke walker it replaced produced the same first limiter ring, so reverting wall_npz to a second reader leaves the test green and only the manual grep in negative-control-durability's sibling negative-control-reuse.log guards the reuse.

item_verdicts.diff: read the four commits against cb373e23: 83c611597 replaces the prior-head lag-one triple with values recomputed from the r-20261115T202148674467 arm, 6cbca9571 replaces the whole-arm versus nova-RMSE comparison with a slice-matched one, 478f5740f adds probe_row_angle and the six tests, and 06f50708c removes the bespoke limiter walk from wall_npz.
item_verdicts.done_when: the arm measurements the done_when names are unchanged by these commits; the gate they gained is scripts/prototypes/drifting_sensor_sequences/probe_rows/test_probe_rows.py, whose after_suite.log records 6 passed with EXIT=0 at 06f50708c and whose negative-control-durability.log records 4 failed with EXIT=1 when the sign of probe_row_angle is reverted.
item_verdicts.goal: the node's goal is the probe-row deliverable, and the four commits gained since cb373e23 (83c611597, 6cbca9571, 478f5740f, 06f50708c) repair the two blocking evidence findings, name the probe projection in scripts/prototypes/drifting_sensor_sequences/probe_rows/study.py:95 and route the wall read through the shared limiter reader at study.py:1004.
item_verdicts.manifest: read; it records the after_suite as 6 passed at 06f50708c, the baseline arm as a scratch tree at eda6cfd6e where the test file does not exist (exit 4) and added_failure_count 0, and its evidence_inputs name imas.cpp:723 as the convention the six tests pin.
item_verdicts.write_paths: the declared paths are docs/evidence/fragments/inverse-equilibrium-baseline/drifting-sensor-probe-rows.html, docs/figures/inverse-equilibrium-baseline/drifting-sensor-sequences and scripts/prototypes/drifting_sensor_sequences, and every path in the four commits is one of the first and the last.

justifications.durability: test_probe_rows.py:46 reddens on a sign flip (negative-control-durability.log records 4 failed, EXIT=1), while test_probe_rows.py:76 derives its expected value from the same wall_units_from_ids call the implementation makes and so stays green under the regression it claims to guard.
justifications.evidence: after_suite.log records 6 passed and EXIT=0 at 06f50708c and the slice-matched numbers at drifting-sensor-probe-rows.html:65 reproduce exactly (0.00935 and 0.00790 against nova 0.0177 and 0.0236), but the prior-head boundary-flux lag-one cells at :44 and :46 read 0.0852 and 0.4537 where the arm's own summary.json and the fragment's stated recipe both give 0.1186 and 0.1866.
justifications.fit: the added code passes ruff check and format and follows the module idiom, but study.py:95 leaves its parameter unannotated while the file's other helpers are typed.
justifications.goal_fidelity: study.py:190 now reads the IMAS probe angle through probe_row_angle and study.py:1005 reads the wall through nova/equilibrium/wall_mask.py:209 as the reuse finding asked, but drifting-sensor-probe-rows.html:46 now carries boundary-flux cells on a different span convention from the rows above it and :49 carries a sentence broken mid-clause.
justifications.reuse: wall_npz now extends nova/equilibrium/wall_mask.py:209, and a search for an owner of the dictionary-angle conversion over nova/, scripts/ and tests/ found only the inlined negation at nova/imas/mast_geometry.py:289, so probe_row_angle restates a machine-local convention rather than forking a shared owner.
justifications.scope_discipline: the four commits touch only docs/evidence/fragments/inverse-equilibrium-baseline/drifting-sensor-probe-rows.html and the two probe_rows modules, both inside the declared paths, though study.py:72-93 carries an unrelated EFIT_CONFIG string reflow.
